correctness.rationale: For all integers q>=1 the Gram inverse is obtained exactly from M=(2D+A)/6. The two symmetry-reduced inverse rows, absolute linear integrals, and vertex convexity characterize all evaluation norms. Three full-symbolic polynomial difference identities have positive-coefficient numerators and positive denominator factors; this proves norming strictness and strict shielding universally. Opposite-sign kernels force strict suboptimality in every edge interior. Coefficient limits give constants 1/6 and 2/3. Direct rational inverses and labelled edge integrals q=1..7 independently corroborate, not replace, universal proof.

value.rationale: The precise K_{2,2,1,...,1} norm is a natural smallest unbalanced multi-defect network projector and complements sharp one-defect and balanced multipartite classes. The four-point norming locus, strict nonmonotone edge-deletion behavior, and third-order cancellation relative to the leading first-order effect yield a structural shielding law, not a routine restatement or a tiny unsupported numerical improvement.
